subject: Follow-up: short responses observed during bulk invoice export — investigation concluded
messages:

Date: 2027-08-10T14:22:00Z
Subject: Short truncated responses during bulk invoice export

Hi Marcus / Monica,

We started a scheduled bulk invoice export yesterday morning and ~2-3% of the generated summaries were abruptly short — they end mid-sentence, e.g. '...charges applied to the invoice are...' and then the response stops. This is causing downstream parsers to error.

We attached a small set of sample payloads and the request-ids we captured from our proxy (fastledger-request-ids.txt). Example request id: fast-req-20270810-8b2a.

Context:
- Model: rdm-3b-v1 (via your hosted endpoint us-east-1)
- Batch size: 250 invoices per call (we use continuous streaming back to our service)
- Time window: Aug 10 04:00–06:00 UTC

Could you check whether Redwood dropped tokens on your side or if there's a known issue with streaming/batching? We're seeing this despite retries.

Thanks — we need a quick triage so we can decide whether to pause exports.

— Elena
Elena Ruiz
Director, Platform Engineering
FastLedger

Subject: Fwd: Re: Short truncated responses during bulk invoice export (internal repro notes)

Forwarding internal repro notes and initial findings.

--- Forwarded message from redwood repro job ---
Job: repro-fastledger-bulk-aug12
Cluster: us-east-1-dedicated-2
Model variant: rdm-3b-v1-q8
Payloads: 300 sample items from sample_payloads.json (same distribution as customer)
Batching: continuous batching enabled (max_batch=512, max_latency=15ms)
Streaming: server stream opened; client simulated with different timeouts (2s, 5s, 10s)

Observations:
- We did not observe server-side truncation or abrupt end-of-streams from the inference engine. All responses reached end-of-generation tokens and closed normally with final token markers.
- A minority (~1.8%) of our simulated clients that used a 3s socket idle timeout saw partial payloads at the client side — the server's stream continued but the simulated client closed the socket, which produced truncated receipts.
- No errors or throttling events in the serving runtime logs (attached excerpt: redwood-trace-20270812.log).
- KV cache metrics and token counts were consistent with expected distributions; no early EOF on the model process.

Log excerpt (normalized):
[2027-08-12T09:12:45Z] request_id=fast-req-20270810-8b2a route=us-east-1 handler=stream start
[2027-08-12T09:12:46Z] request_id=fast-req-20270810-8b2a tokens_generated=412 status=completed final_marker=true
[2027-08-12T09:12:46Z] request_id=fast-req-20270810-8b2a transport=socket client_closed=true (close reason: ECONNRESET)

Recommendation (internal):
- Likely client-side proxy/timeouts are closing the TCP connection before the full stream reaches FastLedger.
- Ask customer to verify proxy idle/read timeouts and confirm they support chunked streaming semantics for long outputs.
- Offer a quick pairing session to reproduce on their environment.

I'll draft the customer-facing summary for Marcus.

— Monica (repro run attached: repro-run-stdout.txt)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@fastledger.com>, ops-team@fastledger.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-15T18:05:00Z
Subject: Investigation update & suggested remediation — FastLedger bulk export

Hi Elena — thanks again for the samples and request ids. Quick summary of our investigation and recommended next steps: 

What we did
- Correlated your request ids with our serving traces (RED-2114).
- Replayed a representative subset of your payloads on our us-east-1 cluster using the same model variant and batching config.
- Instrumented the streaming transport to capture socket-level events and per-request final markers.

What we found
- On the Redwood platform there is no evidence of model or runtime truncation: generation completed to final-token markers in all successful runs. (See attached redwood-trace-20270812.log)
- A small fraction of client connections closed before the server finished streaming full responses. In our repro the behaviour surfaced when the client simulated a 3s idle/read timeout — the server continued but the client socket was closed (client_closed=true).

Likely cause
- The symptoms match an upstream proxy / client-side idle timeout or buffering limit that closes the connection while the server is still streaming the tail of the generation.

Recommended actions for FastLedger
1) Increase the proxy idle/read timeout to >= 15s for export endpoints that expect long outputs.
2) Ensure your proxy supports chunked transfer encoding and forwards partial stream chunks to your downstream consumer.
3) If you prefer, we can run a short pairing session where we stream the same sample from our end into your proxy so we can observe behaviour live.

Next steps & closure
- We're marking the Redwood platform side as "no platform evidence" for truncation. If you update your proxy timeouts and still see truncated outputs, please re-open the ticket or reply here with new request ids.

I've attached the traces and repro stdout we used. Happy to schedule a live debug with your ops team.

Thanks —
